chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Aqeeqa is performed for the child, and his head is shaved when he is seven days old, and his hair is weighed and charity is given in his name equal to the weight of his hair in gold or silver, and the midwife is fed with the leg and the thigh.'
And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Aqeeqa is a camel or a sheep.'

key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: A camel (specifically one that has completed its fourth year)
key_terms.عَقِيقَةٌ: Aqeeqa, the ritual sacrifice offered for a newborn child

ai.seo_question: What are the specific rituals and requirements for performing Aqeeqa on the seventh day for a newborn?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the Sunnah of Aqeeqa on the seventh day, linking the sacrifice to the shaving of the head and the distribution of charity equivalent to the hair's weight in gold or silver. It further specifies the customary gift of meat to the midwife, reflecting the communal gratitude and social welfare aspects of this rite in Shia tradition. The narration clarifies that the sacrifice can be fulfilled with either a sheep or a goat, emphasizing accessibility for families.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘The child, perform Aqeeqa for him, and shave off his head when he is a boy of one seven days, and weigh his hair and give in charity from it by the weight of his hair, gold or silver, and feed the midwife with the leg (of the slaughtered animal) and the leaf (of silver or gold)’.
And heasws said: ‘The Aqeeqa is a camel or sheep’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Khalid and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘For a child Aqiqah must be offered, his head is shaved on the seventh day and equal to the weight of his hairs silver or gold should be given in charity. One leg and hip of the animal slaughtered for ‘Aqiqah should be given to al-Qabilah (the special nurse, doctor).
The animal accepted as ‘Aqiqah can be a badanah (camel) or a sheep.’”
